source.text: Particle 398 of the 2000 drawn with the seed 20261016 from the population of examples/synthetic-triso-population.json: the particle whose kernel peak is nearest the sample's median (kernel peak 928.933 K). The drop across the buffer-to-inner-PyC gap: P / (4 pi R_buffer^2 h) = 0.26858 K for the gap conductance 1.5e5 W/m2/K at the buffer's outer radius 354.356 um. The observed value is the difference of the two patch values of the gap in the solver's output. Tolerance 0.01 K = 1 % of the drop + 0.005 K (FEED's gapDrop check) + (1 - lambda) of the drop (the wedge's gap drop is lambda = 0.999695 times the sphere's), rounded up to 0.005 K, fixed before any run.
source.check: Second method: FEED's own closed form (src/core/trisoSolve.ts, tests/seedOracleTriso.test.ts, to 1e-6 K) and FEED's finite-volume solution; the real solver (FEED_SOLVER=1, tests/seedOracleTriso.test.ts) with every check of the run passing, and its saved output (tests/golden/seed-oracles-triso/) inside the tolerance.
